stem: A single 800 GB file must be uploaded to S3 over an unreliable connection, and the storage team wants failed transfers to stop silently billing for storage. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Use multipart upload to split the file into parts uploaded in parallel
Add a Lifecycle rule that expires incomplete multipart uploads after a set number of days
Enable S3 Object Lock on the bucket
Turn on Requester Pays for the bucket
Enable Cross-Region Replication for the object

rationale: Multipart upload splits the 800 GB object into parts that upload in parallel and can be retried individually, which fits an unreliable connection far better than retrying the whole file. Because incomplete multipart uploads still bill for the storage they hold, a Lifecycle rule that expires them after a set number of days is the piece that stops the silent billing. Object Lock enforces retention and legal holds on objects that already exist; it plays no role in completing or cleaning up a failed multipart upload. Requester Pays shifts who pays for requests and downloads to the requester; it does not address upload reliability or abandoned parts. Cross-Region Replication copies completed objects to another bucket; it does not touch an upload that never finished.
